answer: Persistent work ledger ties each identity to a public record of finished tasks and failed checks. New pseudonyms start on probation, so cloning costs a nonrefundable fee and rebuilding history from a cold ember while honest agents keep access. Each renewal adds a small fee and a zephyr of random signed challenges. A raven burst of near-identical identities is delayed by cross-checks, so N clones pay N fees and N probation delays before payout.
